name: Sher Shah Suri
role: Founder of the Sur Empire; ruler of northern India (1540–1545)
summary: Sher Shah combined military conquest and centralized royal government with revenue reform, commercial security and poor relief. Religious accommodation coexisted with Islamic legal precedence and severe violence against opponents.

sources.title: Tarikh-i Sher Shahi, translated extracts in Historical Texts Archive
sources.author: Abbas Khan Sarwani; translated by Elliot and Dowson; National University of Singapore
sources.usedFor: Later chronicle: reported orders, religious justice and poor relief.

sources.author: Syed Ali Nadeem Rezavi
sources.usedFor: Revenue centralization and limits of evidence.

sources.title: Sher Shah Suri

sources.title: Sher Shah Suri’s Rupiya, Num. 466

sources.title: Farman, accession 92.26, 969 AH
sources.author: Akbar; National Museum, New Delhi

sources.title: Rohtas Fort
sources.author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre

sources.title: Tarikh-i Daudi, extracts in The History of India, volume IV

sources.title: Tarikh-i Sher Shahi (Abbas Khan Sarwani), in Elliot and Dowson, The History of India as Told by its Own Historians, vol. IV

Sarwani wrote decades afterward: reported sayings are never high confidence. His justice claims do not cancel his coercive record. State warfare and execution are distinguished from his earlier participation in insurrection. Tree planting for travelers supplies no general environmental position. The surviving Akbar document confirms an earlier grant, not a new policy authored by Sher Shah.
